messages.author: 2f3428d3166aad1c
messages.subject: Re: load data from sql database
parts:
Landon, that sounds right.

If your data are not that big and in an SQL database, it would be most efficient to read it all in and handle things as R objects.

If your data are huge, you would want to be able to process it with R in a distributed parallel manner, which to my knowledge can’t be done with SQL. For this I mean R running on multiple nodes performing MapReduce operations against an SQL table. In this case as Landon suggests you could iterate through your table and read it in in chunks to a datadr local disk or HDFS connection and go from there.

datadr is a bit different from things like dplyr (which you can use with SQL) because we aren’t restricted to data frames and our fundamental computation unit is MapReduce, which opens up more flexible data structures, more computational possibilities, and the ability to leverage very large-scale systems like Hadoop.

However, there is probably more we can do to make working with SQL databases more simple. If you’d like to discuss or provide more details, we can look into it.

Thanks!

Ryan
